title: Billing health checklist and alert scenarios for QBRs
content:
Purpose:
This is a working worksheet for Customer Success (CS) to use as part of Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) focused on usage economics: token spend, rate limits, budget alerts, and renewal-ready signals. Goal is to give CS a short, repeatable checklist + scenario playbooks so we can quickly assess billing health, escalate risk, and surface upsell/optimization opportunities during QBRs.

How to use this doc (quick):
- Run the data checks in 'Data pulls' 48 hours before a QBR.
- Fill the top-line summary for the account and paste into the QBR slides.
- Walk through the 'Top 3 risk scenarios' if any warning flags pop.
- Save a copy to the customer folder and update 'Last reviewed' in Salesforce.

Top-line summary (one-liner template):
- Current period token spend: $X / month (Y tokens)
- YoY / QoQ change: +/- %
- Active rate limit events (30d): N
- Budget alert hits (90d): M
- Recommended action: [optimize prompts | request Dedicated | increase quota | engage solutions eng]

Metric definitions (standardized):
- Billable tokens: tokens that count toward invoice (generation + input tokens).
- Effective unit cost: invoice amount / billable tokens.
- Rate limit event: any 429 or queued request returned to the customer (count and duration).
- Budget alert: internal system alert firing when projected monthly spend crosses customer-set threshold.

Data pulls & quick SQL snippets (examples):
1) 30-day token spend by model:
SELECT customer_id, model_name, SUM(input_tokens+output_tokens) AS tokens, SUM(billed_amount) as spend
FROM billing.events
WHERE customer_id = '<<CUSTOMER_ID>>' AND event_ts >= current_date - interval '30 days'
GROUP BY customer_id, model_name
ORDER BY tokens DESC;

2) Rate limit events (last 60 days):
SELECT count(*) as rate_limit_hits, sum(duration_ms) as total_backoff_ms
FROM infra.request_logs
WHERE customer_id='<<CUSTOMER_ID>>' AND response_code=429 AND event_ts >= current_date - interval '60 days';

Quick health checks (pass/fail style):
- Token spend rising faster than product usage? (compare tokens per active user month-over-month)
- Effective unit cost > 2x expected band for similar workload?
- Recurrent budget alerts or manual spend overrides in the last 90d?
- Any sustained 429s or customer-reported latency spikes?
If >=2 checks fail -> mark as billing risk and escalate.

Top 3 risk scenarios and playbooks:
1) Rapid token spend growth (unexpected):
  Symptoms: >50% MoM token growth, customer didn't increase seats/features, multiple spike days.
  Possible causes: bad prompt loop, cron jobs, fine-tune gone wrong, third-party integration misconfigured.
  Playbook:
    - Step 1: Confirm the tokens-by-endpoint breakdown (we want which API route/model).
    - Step 2: Ask PM/engineer for recent deploys / PRs in the customer integration window. Linked ticket: JIRA-INV-3421.
    - Step 3: Recommend immediate mitigations: turn on rate cap, set daily budget alerts, reduce max_tokens in generation calls.
    - Step 4: If >=100% over forecast and customer is sensitive to cost, propose a dedicated or reserved plan with predictable pricing (ops to prepare cost model).
    - Slack template (to customer):
      "Hi {contact}, we noticed unexpected usage on {dates}. We've temporarily suggested throttling to avoid invoice surprises. Can we schedule 20m to review root cause?"

2) Budget alerts firing repeatedly (administrative):
  Symptoms: alert threshold hit >2 times in 30d, customer hits manual override.
  Playbook:
    - Step 1: Validate billing contact and threshold setup in the console.
    - Step 2: Walk through chargeback: which teams, which projects are driving spikes? Pull project tag report.
    - Step 3: Educate customer on budget policies and recommended thresholds. Offer to set up automatic soft caps.
    - Step 4: Suggest tagging/labeling migrations to better attribute spend.

3) Persistent rate limits impacting UX:
  Symptoms: repeated 429s, customer escalations to support, or backoff-related latency >3s added to requests.
  Playbook:
    - Step 1: Confirm spike pattern and whether it coincides with peak load windows.
    - Step 2: If request size is high, recommend batching tweaks or smaller max tokens.
    - Step 3: Short-term: enable higher throughput tier for X hours while debugging (if entitled).
    - Step 4: Long-term: propose Dedicated or burst capacity; involve Solutions Eng to size.
    - Escalation path: CS -> Solutions Eng -> Pricing -> SRE. Link to escalation doc: CONFLUENCE-1234

Renewal signals to capture during QBR (billing-focused):
- Positive signals: steady or increasing spend within forecast, adoption across >1 product line, willingness to sign a commit for reserved capacity.
- Risk signals: unpredictable surges, repeated billing disputes, manual overrides, or customer using free-trial / promo credits and nearing expiration.
- Action items tied to signals: prepare pricing options, schedule technical health check with solutions eng, create a cost-optimization engagement.

Sample slides content (copy-paste to QBR slide):
- Slide title: Billing health snapshot
- Bullet: Last 30d tokens: Y (change +Z%)
- Bullet: Avg unit cost: $A per 1k tokens (bench: $B)
- Bullet: Alerts: budget=M, rate_limit=N
- Recommendation: [Conservative: enable soft cap] / [Growth: discuss dedicated capacity]

Alert thresholds (recommended starting points):
- Soft budget email alert: 70% of monthly forecast
- Hard budget notification to CS: 90% of forecast
- Auto-throttle (if enabled): 105% projected monthly spend
- Rate limit escalation: >10 429s in 24h or >5% of requests throttled for 7d
Note: thresholds are customer-specific; use these as starting defaults during QBR prep.

Ownership & handoffs:
- CS owner: update QBR notes and set next check date in Salesforce.
- If remediation requires infra changes: file a support ticket and tag SRE on the ticket.
- Solutions Eng involvement: required when proposing Dedicated/reserved plans or for throughput tuning.

Open questions / TODOs (for this template):
- Add more granular per-route cost attribution (engineering TODO: expose in billing API).
- Define a standard 'cost-sensitivity' score to help prioritize accounts for proactive outreach.
- Draft an email playbook for manual override scenarios (who approves and process).

Appendix: useful links & quick references:
- Billing API docs: https://internal.redwood/billing-api
- Console: customer quota & alerts page (link to account)
- Escalation doc: CONFLUENCE-1234
- Last related JIRA: JIRA-INV-3421

Notes to self (working):

- Need to validate SQL against prod schema (test on staging first).
